entries.verdict: Ravenwing speed, shoot-and-move pressure, plasma and D6+1 guns make this a textbook hard fast-shooting matchup.
entries.playerPlan: Refuse long lanes, do not chase bikes and use objectives to force one wing close enough for Wraiths to tag while the missile stays hidden.
entries.army: Space Marines with access to durable elite infantry and highly mobile Ravenwing shooting.
entries.opponentPlan: A mobile build can create cross-board angles, shoot and reposition while a hard melee unit controls the centre.
entries.kaashifPlan: Do not chase skirmishers across open lanes. Hide the support package, force the bikes toward objectives and launch only when the Wraiths can trap them.
entries.evidence: Based on the submitted Brighton list and current 11th-edition datasheets.

entries.team: The boys go to Brighton for “Warhammer”
entries.verdict: Mobile Lokhust shooting plus Void Dragon and other mortal/high-damage spikes threaten the C’tan plan while the Necron shell remains hard to clear.
entries.playerPlan: Use terrain to deny Lokhust angles, keep the missile compact and commit the Void Dragon only when it can trade into the opposing vehicles or C’tan without being focused.
entries.army: Another durable Necron build built around resilient threats, regeneration and efficient objective play.
entries.opponentPlan: It will try to win the durability race, force awkward target priority and preserve expensive threats until late.
entries.kaashifPlan: Concentrate damage instead of splitting, protect Technomancers from character-killing tools and use the Void Dragon where it can punish vehicles or an opposing C’tan safely.
entries.evidence: Based on the submitted Brighton list and current 11th-edition datasheets.

entries.team: The boys go to Brighton for “Warhammer”
entries.verdict: A board full of fast War Dogs with melta, autocannons and D6+2 melee can shoot while staying difficult to pin.
entries.playerPlan: Hide all C’tan from the opening spear lanes, threaten multiple dog charges with Wraiths and avoid trading a whole brick for one cheap hull.
entries.army: A vehicle-heavy army of fast War Dogs with efficient shooting, melee and high objective pressure.
entries.opponentPlan: They spread onto firing angles, trade individual hulls and use melta/high-damage guns to pressure C’tan.
entries.kaashifPlan: Hide until several dogs can be tagged at once. Avoid isolated C’tan exposures and make the Wraith charges shut down guns, not just score a trade.
entries.evidence: Based on the submitted Brighton list and current 11th-edition datasheets.

entries.team: The boys go to Brighton for “Warhammer”
entries.verdict: This Custodes list wants a direct melee contest and has comparatively few bodies, which suits the Wraith screen and counter-charge plan.
entries.playerPlan: Make them spend an elite unit to clear Wraiths, protect Technomancers from the Blade Champion and concentrate the missile on one brick.
entries.army: Elite melee infantry with excellent saves, strong character-led units and relatively few bodies.
entries.opponentPlan: They usually take the centre, force close combats and win by making each model hard to shift.
entries.kaashifPlan: The fight is catchable and mostly comes to you. Preserve the Technomancers from Precision, layer Wraiths in front and counter-charge after they commit.
entries.evidence: Based on the submitted Brighton list and current 11th-edition datasheets.

entries.verdict: Unknown Orks are still likely to bring pressure into the counter-charge zone, but the absence of a list lowers confidence.
entries.playerPlan: Check for Scout, transports and character Precision, then screen the first wave and keep the missile together behind the Wraiths.
entries.army: A high-volume pressure army with fast melee, large units, transports and disruptive forward pieces.
entries.opponentPlan: It wants to occupy lanes early, pin the army in deployment and deliver several charges at once.
entries.kaashifPlan: This is a preferred shape: block Scout moves when needed, let Wraiths absorb the first contact and counter-charge the committed mass with the compact missile.
entries.evidence: No list was submitted; this is a faction-level provisional read.

entries.verdict: Unknown T’au remain a bad structural matchup because mobile guns can avoid the slow melee package.
entries.playerPlan: Deploy without visible C’tan or Technomancers, then force the actual list to contest several objectives inside Wraith charge distance.
entries.army: Fast, efficient shooting with battlesuits, skimmers, rail weapons and disposable spotting or screening units.
entries.opponentPlan: They create firing angles, focus one durable target and reposition so the counter-charge cannot connect.
entries.kaashifPlan: This is the worst archetype for Kaashif. Stage completely out of sight, pressure several objectives together and use Wraiths to trap suits or vehicles before revealing C’tan.
entries.evidence: No list was submitted; this is a faction-level provisional read.

entries.verdict: Unknown Thousand Sons still imply dangerous mortal wounds, psychic Devastating Wounds and teleport play.
entries.playerPlan: Confirm the actual cabal package, screen landing zones and never rely on Necrodermis alone against direct mortal or Devastating Wound output.
entries.army: Elite psychic shooting with teleport tools, Devastating Wounds and direct mortal-wound effects.
entries.opponentPlan: They isolate a valuable unit, amplify psychic damage and use movement tricks to avoid the counter-charge.
entries.kaashifPlan: Respect Doombolt and psychic Devastating Wounds even when normal line-of-sight maths looks safe. Spread threat pressure, deny teleport landing zones and do not expose Technomancers.
entries.evidence: No list was submitted; this is a faction-level provisional read.

entries.verdict: The Blood Angels melee is welcome, but two Vindicators, speeders and haywire add serious high-damage shooting and mortal wounds.
entries.playerPlan: Hide C’tan from Vindicator lanes, protect Technomancers from the Scout sniper and counter-charge jump units only after the shooting pieces are pinned or screened.
entries.army: Fast Space Marine melee pressure backed by jump units, transports and a smaller shooting package.
entries.opponentPlan: They threaten an early multi-charge, use speed to choose a flank and try to kill support characters during the scrum.
entries.kaashifPlan: This is broadly the kind of matchup Kaashif wants: receive the first wave with Wraiths, protect the Technomancers, then counter-charge with the missile.
entries.evidence: Based on the submitted Brighton list and current 11th-edition datasheets.
